head.name: @fzlt/core/scene
head.lead: An animation recipe as data. A scene is JSON: a **stage** (a fixed pixel grid fitted to the box, a background, a starfield, shake, the clock), a **cast** (sprites, rects, text and lines, drawn in order, each value a number, a track or a blink on the scene clock), the **cues** (one-shot fx moments: a pop word, a kick, a burst) and the **gags** (a running bit: an fx emitter held open over a window, following a track). One player runs them all, so a gallery entry ships its data, not its own code. Bricks: the kernel (fps cap, settle), @fzlt/core/fx (particles, words, shake), @fzlt/core/sprite (pixel art, baked once), @fzlt/core/timeline's easings, and @fzlt/core/slot (scene(data) is a slot mount). The contract: time moves in the step on numbers only (no DOM, no allocation); one canvas, added through the ledger, so destroy() gives the page back exactly; after end seconds it rests on the last frame and the engine settles (busy(sec) holds it awake until then); a tap plays it again. With reduced motion it draws the poster frame (no cues, no gags) and settles.

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

items.doc: A value on the scene clock t (seconds): - a number or a string (a colour): constant; - a track [from, to, at, dur, ease?]: from until at, then eased to to over dur seconds (an EASES name, default "linear"); dur 0 jumps once t is past at, and works on strings; - a blink { blink: [a, b], hz, on?: [from, to], then? }: a before from; inside the window b on odd ticks of hz per second, a on even ones; then (default a) from to on.
